purpose: The Swiss-army knife for Linux networking config — replaces ifconfig, route, arp, netstat link table. Talks to kernel via NETLINK_ROUTE. OBJECT is one of: address, link, route, neighbour, rule, netns, tunnel, addrlabel, l2tp, fou, macsec, monitor, mptcp, mroute, mrule, sr, vrf, xfrm. Most subcommands have their own man page (ip-address, ip-link, ip-route, ip-neighbour, etc). For the JSON-friendly machine-readable output, add `-j` (often `-j -p` for pretty-printed).

flags.name: -s, --stats, --statistics
flags.doc: Output more statistics (e.g. ip -s link shows rx/tx counters).

flags.name: -d, --details
flags.doc: Output more details (e.g. ip -d link shows driver info).

flags.name: -r, --resolve
flags.doc: Use system resolver to print DNS names.

flags.name: -f, --family
flags.doc: Restrict to a single address family.

flags.name: -j, --json
flags.doc: JSON output. Pair with -p for pretty-printing.

flags.name: -p, --pretty
flags.doc: Pretty-print JSON or other formatted output.

flags.name: -N, --Numeric
flags.doc: Print interface/route table indices as numbers (skip name resolution).

flags.name: -n, --netns
flags.doc: Run in the network namespace named NAME (under /var/run/netns/).

flags.name: -a, --all
flags.doc: Operate on all objects (e.g. with `link`, all interfaces).

examples.expected_output: JSON describing eth0's addresses, MAC, MTU, state
examples.scenario: Machine-readable interface state for scripts.
Determine which interface and gateway will be used for a destination.
Inspect a persistent network namespace's interfaces from the host.

command: ip link { add | delete | set | show | help } [DEV] [TYPE]
purpose: Manage L2 network devices — physical NICs, virtual interfaces (veth, bridge, vlan, vxlan, tun, tap, bond, dummy, gre, ipip, sit, geneve, wireguard). Where you bring interfaces up/down, set MAC, MTU, state, attach to bridges, configure namespaces.

flags.name: add NAME type TYPE
flags.doc: Create a new virtual interface. TYPE = bridge|veth|vlan|vxlan|bond|tun|tap|dummy|geneve|wireguard|... (each type has its own option set).

flags.name: set DEV mtu N
flags.doc: Set MTU bytes (typical 1500; jumbo 9000; tunnels need lower).

flags.name: set DEV netns NS
flags.doc: Move interface into network namespace NS.

flags.name: set DEV type bond mode MODE
show [DEV]
flags.doc: Display interfaces. Without DEV, all of them.

flags.name: add link PARENT name CHILD type vlan id N
flags.doc: Create VLAN subinterface. e.g. `ip link add link eth0 name eth0.10 type vlan id 10`.

flags.name: add type veth peer name OTHER
flags.doc: Create veth pair (one end DEV, other named OTHER).

flags.name: add NAME type vxlan id VNI dstport 4789 dev DEV

examples.invocation: ip link add veth0 type veth peer name veth1 && ip link set veth1 netns ns1
examples.expected_output: veth0 in host, veth1 in netns ns1
examples.scenario: Wire a network namespace to the host with a veth pair (the manual way to do what containers do).
Lower MTU on an interface running over a tunnel that adds overhead.

examples.expected_output: bridge details: stp_state, vlan_filtering, hello_time, etc.
examples.scenario: Inspect Docker's default bridge config in detail.

command: ip address { add | del | flush | show } [DEV]
purpose: Manage IPv4/IPv6 addresses on interfaces. Add/remove/list addresses, peer addresses, broadcasts, scopes, lifetimes (for DHCP/SLAAC).

flags.name: add ADDR/PREFIX dev DEV
flags.doc: Add an address. e.g. `ip addr add 10.0.0.1/24 dev eth0`.

flags.name: show [DEV]
flags.doc: Display addresses. Default shows all interfaces.

flags.name: show dynamic / permanent
flags.doc: Filter by SLAAC dynamic vs manually configured.

flags.name: add ... scope SCOPE
flags.doc: global|link|host. Default 'global'. 'host' is loopback-style; 'link' = same L2 only.

flags.name: add ... noprefixroute
flags.doc: Don't auto-add a /PREFIX route — useful when you'll add it manually.

flags.name: add ... mngtmpaddr
flags.doc: For SLAAC: managed temporary address (RFC 4941 privacy extensions).

examples.expected_output: silent on success; visible in `ip addr show eth0`
examples.scenario: Statically configure an IPv4 address on an interface.

examples.expected_output: global IPv6 addresses on all interfaces
examples.scenario: Find all routable IPv6 addresses on the host.
Wipe interface config before re-applying.

command: ip route { add | del | replace | get | show | flush } [DEST]
purpose: Manage routing-table entries. Add/remove/inspect routes, evaluate which route a packet would take, manipulate the multiple routing tables, set per-route metric/MTU/source.

flags.name: add DEST via GW
flags.doc: Add a route. e.g. `ip route add 10.0.0.0/8 via 192.168.1.1`.

flags.name: add default via GW
flags.doc: Add default gateway. (Equivalent to `add 0.0.0.0/0 via GW`.)

flags.name: get DEST
flags.doc: Evaluate which route would be used for DEST. Useful for debugging policy routing.

flags.name: show [DEST]
flags.doc: Display routes. Without DEST, all of main table.

flags.name: show table TABLE
flags.doc: From a specific table (named in /etc/iproute2/rt_tables, indexed 0-255). 'main', 'local', 'default' are defaults.

flags.name: add ... src SRC
flags.doc: Override source address selection for this route.

flags.name: add ... mtu MTU
flags.doc: Override MTU for this route (PMTUD result).

flags.name: add ... proto PROTO
flags.doc: Which protocol added this route (kernel|boot|static|dhcp|ra|...). Filter with `proto static` to see manual entries.

flags.name: add ... onlink
flags.doc: Pretend gateway is directly attached (skip ARP for it). Useful for VPN setups.

flags.name: add ... nexthop
flags.doc: For ECMP / multipath: `add ... nexthop via GW1 weight 1 nexthop via GW2 weight 1`.

examples.scenario: Determine egress interface for a destination.
Route a subnet through a VPN interface.
Inspect a policy-routing table for multi-homed setup.

command: ip neighbour { add | del | change | replace | show | flush } [ADDR]
purpose: Manage the ARP/NDP cache (kernel's IP→MAC mapping). 'ip neigh' = synonym. Replaces the legacy `arp` command.

flags.name: add ADDR lladdr MAC dev DEV
change ADDR lladdr MAC dev DEV
replace ADDR lladdr MAC dev DEV
show [ADDR] [dev DEV]
flags.doc: Display cache. Without args, all entries on all interfaces.

examples.scenario: List learned MAC addresses on local network.
Force re-ARP after a host's MAC changed.
Debug IPv6 connectivity at the link layer.

purpose: Configure Linux bridges beyond what `ip link` exposes — STP, per-port flags, FDB (forwarding database = MAC table), MDB (multicast), VLAN filtering, group_fwd_mask. The detailed-bridge-config CLI.

flags.name: link show
flags.doc: Per-bridge-port detail (state, designated root, port id, etc.).

flags.name: link set dev DEV mcast_router N
link set dev DEV learning on/off
link set dev DEV flood on/off
link set dev DEV hairpin on/off
flags.doc: Allow hairpin (forward back out same port). Required for container-to-self via published port.

flags.name: link set dev DEV root_block on
vlan add vid VID dev DEV
flags.doc: VLAN-filtering: tag a port with VID.

flags.name: monitor
flags.doc: Watch FDB/MDB changes in real time.

examples.scenario: See what MACs the bridge has learned (debug L2 forwarding).

examples.invocation: bridge link set dev veth0 hairpin on
examples.scenario: Enable hairpin so a container can reach its own published port.

examples.invocation: bridge vlan add vid 10 dev eth1 pvid untagged
examples.scenario: Configure VLAN-aware bridge port.

purpose: Configure netfilter rules (legacy front-end). Tables: filter (default), nat, mangle, raw, security. Chains: INPUT, OUTPUT, FORWARD, PREROUTING, POSTROUTING, plus user-defined. Operates on rules within chains; first match wins (unless target returns).

flags.name: -L [CHAIN]
flags.doc: List rules. Combine with -n (no DNS), -v (verbose), --line-numbers, -x (exact counters).

flags.name: -F [CHAIN]
flags.doc: Flush all rules in chain (or all chains).

flags.name: -P CHAIN POLICY
flags.doc: Set default policy for built-in chain (ACCEPT|DROP|REJECT).

flags.name: --sport / --dport
flags.doc: Source/dest port (for tcp/udp). Range with colon.

flags.name: -m MATCH
flags.doc: Load extension match module (state, conntrack, recent, limit, multiport, owner, etc.). See iptables-extensions(8).

flags.name: -g CHAIN
flags.doc: Goto user chain (vs jump — RETURN goes to caller's caller).

examples.expected_output: rules with packet/byte counters and position numbers
examples.scenario: Diagnose a firewall — see counters tick to identify the matching rule.
Set up a port forward (what `docker -p 80:8080` does behind the scenes).
Allow return traffic (the cornerstone of a stateful firewall — usually first rule).

purpose: Modern netfilter front-end. Single CLI for IPv4/IPv6/ARP/bridge/netdev rules. Atomic ruleset replace, sets/maps, named chains, easier syntax than iptables. Default on RHEL 8+, Debian 11+.

flags.name: -a, --handle
flags.doc: Show rule handles in list output (needed for `delete rule ... handle N`).

flags.name: add chain FAMILY TABLE NAME { type T hook HOOK priority P; policy P; }
flags.doc: Create chain hooked to netfilter. e.g. `add chain inet filter input { type filter hook input priority 0; policy drop; }`.

flags.name: add rule FAMILY TABLE CHAIN EXPR VERDICT
flags.doc: Append rule. EXPR = match expression (ip/ip6/tcp/udp/ct/meta/...). VERDICT = accept|drop|reject|jump CHAIN|return.

flags.name: delete rule FAMILY TABLE CHAIN handle N
flags.doc: Delete by handle (use `list ruleset -a` to see handles).

flags.name: add set ... { type T; flags F; ... }
flags.doc: Create a named set. e.g. `add set inet filter blocklist { type ipv4_addr; flags interval; }`.

examples.expected_output: entire current ruleset in nft DSL
examples.scenario: Show all current netfilter rules (cleaner than iptables -L).

examples.invocation: nft add rule inet filter input ip saddr 10.0.0.0/8 accept
examples.scenario: Allow traffic from a CIDR.
Programmatic firewall inspection (e.g. by config-mgmt tools).

purpose: Capture and display packets on an interface using libpcap. The Swiss-army knife for network debugging. FILTER is a libpcap BPF expression. Requires CAP_NET_RAW (or root). Outputs human-readable summary by default; `-w FILE` saves a pcap.

flags.name: -n
flags.doc: Don't resolve addresses to names (faster, less DNS pollution).

flags.name: -A
flags.doc: ASCII dump only (good for HTTP debugging).

flags.name: -w FILE
flags.doc: Write to pcap file (binary format wireshark/tshark can read).

flags.name: -s SNAPLEN
flags.doc: Bytes per packet to capture (0 = full packet, default in modern tcpdump).

flags.name: -C MEGABYTES
flags.doc: With -w, rotate file after N MB.

flags.name: -W COUNT
flags.doc: With -C, keep only COUNT files (ring buffer).

flags.name: -Z USER
flags.doc: Drop privileges to USER after opening interface.

flags.name: -j TIMESTAMP-TYPE
flags.doc: Set timestamp source (host, host_lowprec, adapter, adapter_unsynced).

flags.name: -K
flags.doc: Skip checksum verification (avoids false 'bad cksum' on TX-offloaded NICs).

examples.scenario: Watch for incoming HTTP connections.
Capture all traffic to/from 10.0.0.5 across any interface for offline wireshark analysis.
Filter for connection-significant packets only.

purpose: Socket statistics. Replaces netstat. Reads /proc/net via NETLINK; faster than netstat at scale. Default lists established TCP. Filters: state, src/dst address+port, owning UID/process, protocol.

flags.name: -a
flags.doc: All states (default = ESTABLISHED only for TCP).

flags.name: -p
flags.doc: Show owning process (needs root for non-own sockets).

flags.name: -i
flags.doc: TCP info (cwnd, rtt, retransmits — like `tcp_info` from getsockopt).

flags.name: -K
flags.doc: Forcibly close matching sockets (TCP RST). Requires root.

flags.name: state STATE
flags.doc: Filter to TCP state (established, syn-sent, time-wait, close-wait, etc.).

examples.expected_output: all listening TCP sockets with owning process
examples.scenario: Find what's listening on port X (the universal 'who's running on :8080?' question).
Inspect TCP performance per active connection.
Quick overview of socket counts by family/state.

purpose: DNS lookup tool, the gold-standard debugging interface. Defaults: query default resolver for A record. Verbose output includes question/answer/authority/additional sections, query time, server, flags. Plus-options control behavior (+short, +trace, +dnssec, +tcp, etc.).

flags.name: TYPE
flags.doc: Record type: A | AAAA | CNAME | MX | NS | PTR | SOA | SRV | TXT | ANY | AXFR | etc.

flags.name: +short
flags.doc: Just the answer values, no envelope. (Best for scripts.)

flags.name: +trace
flags.doc: Iterative resolution from root (good for diagnosing delegation issues).

flags.name: +dnssec
flags.doc: Set DO bit and show RRSIG records.

flags.name: +tcp
flags.doc: Force TCP transport (for large responses or testing).

flags.name: +norecurse
flags.doc: Don't set RD bit (ask authoritative server directly).

flags.name: +noall +answer
flags.doc: Show only the ANSWER section (cleaner than +short for multi-record results).

flags.name: +nssearch
flags.doc: Find SOA via NSes for the zone (consistency check across NSes).

examples.scenario: Quick A-record lookup for scripts.

examples.expected_output: iterative resolution showing root → .com → example.com NS → answer
examples.scenario: Debug DNS delegation problems.
Reverse-lookup an IP.

purpose: Query system databases via the NSS (name service switch) layer. Goes through nsswitch.conf — exactly the same path getaddrinfo() and friends take. Useful for testing NSS configuration without writing C.

flags.name: DATABASE
flags.doc: passwd | group | hosts | networks | services | protocols | rpc | ethers | shadow | gshadow | aliases | initgroups | netgroup.

flags.name: -s SERVICE
flags.doc: Override nsswitch source for this lookup (e.g. `-s files` to skip DNS).

flags.name: -i
flags.doc: Read NSS-database config and exit (debug NSS module load).

examples.scenario: Test full NSS resolution path (files+dns+resolved+...) — what an app's getaddrinfo would actually return.
Read user info via NSS (works regardless of whether passwd is in files, ldap, sssd, ...).
Look up service-name ↔ port from /etc/services.

purpose: Inspect/manipulate the kernel connection tracking table. Lists tracked flows, kills entries, watches events in real time, dumps stats. The diagnostic for stateful firewall and NAT issues.

examples.expected_output: all tracked TCP connections to port 80
examples.scenario: See active HTTP connections (via the firewall's view).
Real-time observation of connection-tracking events — useful for debugging NAT or middlebox behavior.
Quick check of conntrack table size vs nf_conntrack_max sysctl.

purpose: Network discovery and security scanner. Port scan, service/version detection, OS fingerprint, scriptable via NSE. Outbound-traffic intensive; use with permission.

flags.name: -sS
flags.doc: SYN scan (stealth, default for root). Sends SYN, sees SYN-ACK = open, RST = closed, no response = filtered.

flags.name: -sT
flags.doc: TCP connect scan (no root needed; full handshake).

flags.name: -p PORTS
flags.doc: Port range. e.g. -p 22,80,443 or -p 1-1000 or -p- for all 65535.

flags.name: -Pn
flags.doc: Skip ping (assume host is up — useful behind firewalls that drop ICMP).

flags.name: -T<0-5>
flags.doc: Timing template (0=paranoid, 5=insane). Higher = more parallelism + shorter timeouts.

flags.name: -oN / -oX / -oG / -oA
flags.doc: Output format: normal | XML | grepable | all three.

flags.name: --script SCRIPT
flags.doc: NSE script(s). Categories: default, safe, intrusive, vuln, brute, discovery, etc.

flags.name: --top-ports N
flags.doc: Scan only the top N most common ports.

flags.name: --reason
flags.doc: Show why nmap classified each port the way it did.

examples.scenario: Quick service inventory of a host.
Network-wide host enumeration without port scanning.
Detailed audit of a single target with all output formats saved.
